cards.text: Don't get in if your ride arrives early.
My husband pulled up outside the station, waving, then texted: "Leaving home now."
Through the windscreen, he kept smiling and patting the empty passenger seat.
I rang him. He answered from our kitchen, the kettle whistling behind him.
In the car, his lips moved along with every word, perfectly in time.
I hung up and hid in the ticket hall until the car rolled away.
Right on time, his headlights swept the station, and I climbed in, shaking.
He smiled. "You didn't get in last time."
